figures.caption: Per-slice wall of the tracked read at the diverted 550-cell state on one H200, against the number of slices in the batch. The dotted line is the 0.2 ms bound; the series is the minimum of 20 steady-state calls at each batch size.

rubric.contrast: defect: the bound's text and dotted line are grey #929292 on white, a contrast ratio of about 3.1:1 (measured pixel value 146,146,146), below the 4.5:1 that 14 pt text needs to pass AA; the annotation naming the figure's central threshold is the faintest text on the page
rubric.data_ink: pass: a single blue 3 pt series with markers carries the picture and is the only plotted data; its batch-16 value is directly labelled; the sole ruled element is the bound line the caption names
rubric.decoration: pass: no gridlines, no background fill, no gradient and no shading; the top and right spines are absent and only the two scaled axes are drawn
rubric.label_collision: pass: the direct label '9.379 ms at 16' clears both the line and its marker at batch 16, the bottom-left bound label clears the '1' tick label and the y-axis, and no text is clipped at any edge, with both axis labels complete
rubric.legibility: defect: the falling per-slice series reads at a glance (about 54.6 ms at 1 slice to 5.8 ms at 64), but the 0.2 ms bound the figure is built around cannot be located - on a 0-to-about-65 ms linear y-axis the dotted reference line renders 2 px above the black x-axis spine (measured at row 654 against the spine at row 656 of a 720 px canvas), so it reads as a second faint baseline rather than a threshold roughly 29x below the last point
rubric.table_form: pass: four ordered batch sizes plotted as a falling relationship, not a lookup table; the same four rows are carried as a table in the fragment above the figure

findings.summary: The 0.2 ms bound is drawn by axhline at y=0.2 on an axis whose top is max(per_slice)*1.2 (line 64), about 65 ms, so the dotted reference line renders 2 px above the black x-axis spine (row 654 vs spine row 656) and is visually indistinguishable from the axis. The figure exists to show that no batch size reaches the bound; the gap it is about - a factor near 29 at 64 slices and 47 at 16 - is the one quantity the panel cannot show, and the caption's 'The dotted line is the 0.2 ms bound' points a reader at a line that looks like the axis. A log y-scale, or a stated break, would let the bound and the data share one panel. Reported, not edited, under this review's read-only fence.

The bound label and its dotted line use GREY (#929292) at 14 pt on white, about 3.1:1 contrast against the 4.5:1 text at that size needs to pass AA. Grey is right for a reference mark, but here it is applied to the only text that states the bound's value, making the figure's central reference the faintest mark on the page; the dotted line inherits the same weakness.

The x-axis is set to log base 2 with integer tick labels at 1, 4, 16 and 64, so the four points are spaced equidistantly even though the batch multiplies fourfold between each. The axis label reads only 'slices per batch' and gives no log indication, so a reader can misread the equal horizontal steps as equal increments and overestimate how soon the wall stops improving. Labelling the axis as logarithmic, or annotating the fourfold steps, would prevent the misread; the falling direction and the plotted points remain readable, so this does not block.
